GENERAL FUND AMENDMENT RATIONALE. REVENUE EXPECTATIONS. Comparing 2025-2026 original to 2025-2026 Amendment #1 with the difference: Enrollment 12,074.00 to 12,071.23, a difference of (2.77); Foundation 130,230,164 to 130,788,472, a difference of 558,308; 27L(4) MPSERS 0 to 1,326,153, a difference of 1,326,153; 147A(1) MPSERS 1,007,246 to 0, a difference of (1,007,246); 35(A) Early Literacy 176,655 to 0, a difference of (176,655).

MPSERS UPDATES, FISCAL YEAR 2025. The state provided 147a(4) funds to offset retirement expenses in the amount of $5,055,278. That funding would be eliminated for fiscal year 2026. The presentation stresses that the payment was a categorical payment that does not roll into future foundation allowance and was essentially one-time money.

MPSERS UPDATES, FISCAL YEAR 2026. The state eliminated 147a(1) at the last minute, a loss shown as ($1,007,246). Grant expenditure budgets must be adjusted to reflect final allocations and approved state grant budgets. The salary adjustment reflects the actual attrition sustained compared to the original goal, and within the salary adjustment are adjustments to stipends, longevity, and similar items. Retirement adjustments reflect actual attrition plus the increase in retirement costs for TSD that was not anticipated.

2026_339_updates_to_cdb_2026_2.paragraph: Summary of the annual revisions to the Troy School District High School Course Description Book for the 2026/2027 school year, prepared as a OneTroy document by administrators and department heads from both high schools with the Teaching and Learning team. Eleven new courses are added, including AP Business with Personal Finance, AP Cybersecurity, AP Precalculus AB and AP Precalculus BC, plus six semester-long English 11 electives, Mathematics of Tabletop Games, Sports Officiating and a Career Capstone. Eleven courses in Social Studies, English and Life Skills are removed because none has run in the past five years, Achievement Skills III is renamed Integrated Studies III, and the book's format changes from PDF to PaperTurn.
2026_339_updates_to_cdb_2026_2.page:
**Purpose**
The High School Course Description Book (CDB) shows course requirements and elective opportunities for students, organized by department so students and families understand the offerings. It is a OneTroy document developed collaboratively by administrators and department heads from both high schools along with the Teaching and Learning team, and is updated annually as part of the curriculum review process. Department teams determine where descriptions should be updated to reflect new curriculum and instruction and where courses should be added or deleted. The changes listed apply to the 2026/2027 school year.

**Courses added**

| Course | Grades | Length / credit |
|---|---|---|
| AP Business with Personal Finance | 9-12 | Full year, 1.0 credit |
| AP Cybersecurity | 9-12 | Full year, 1.0 credit |
| AP Precalculus AB | 9-12 | Full year, 1.0 credit |
| AP Precalculus BC | 9-12 | Full year, 1.0 credit |
| Career Capstone | 11-12 | 1 semester, 1/2 credit |
| English 11 1 - Great American Stories | 11 | 1 semester, 0.5 credit |
| English 11 1 - Contemporary American Literature | 11 | 1 semester, 0.5 credit |
| English 11 1 - American Dramas and Musicals | 11 | 1 semester, 0.5 credit |
| English 11 2 - Persuasive Writing | 11 | 1 semester, 0.5 credit |
| English 11 2 - Writing Imaginative Fiction | 11 | 1 semester, 0.5 credit |
| English 11 2 - Writing Personal Memoirs | 11 | 1 semester, 0.5 credit |
| Mathematics of Tabletop Games | 11-12 | 1 semester, 0.5 credit |
| Sports Officiating | 9-12 | 1 semester, 0.5 credit |

**Course replacement notes**
AP Cybersecurity replaces and builds upon the previously offered Cybersecurity course and is part of the AP Career Kickstart group. AP Precalculus AB replaces the previously offered Precalculus; AP Precalculus BC replaces the previously offered Honors Precalculus. Both AP Precalculus courses require completion of Algebra 2. AP Business with Personal Finance satisfies 1 credit of the math related graduation requirement; Mathematics of Tabletop Games satisfies 0.5 credit of the math related graduation requirement and requires Geometry.

**English 11 structure**
Semester 1 is Literary Analysis in Reading; Writing about Reading, with students choosing one of three courses. Semester 2 is Writing with a Purpose and Exploring Mentor Texts, again choosing one of three. All six include focused sessions tied to the SAT.

**Courses removed** (none of these offerings has run in the past five years)
Social Studies: Political Science, Stories of Yourself and Others, Psychology 2, Conflicts of the 20th Century, Philosophy. English: Literature of Suspense, Science Fiction, Voices in Literature, Modern Shakespeare. Life Skills: Interior Design, Stitchery.

**Other changes**
Achievement Skills III will now be called Integrated Studies III; increased math-related and NCAA course approvals; the format changed from PDF to PaperTurn.
2026_339_updates_to_cdb_2026_2.verbose:
Administrative memorandum describing updates to the Troy School District High School Course Description Book (CDB) for the 2026/2027 school year. The CDB shows the course requirements and elective opportunities for students and is organized by department so that students and families understand the offerings. It is described as a OneTroy document developed collaboratively by administrators and department heads from both high schools along with the Teaching and Learning team, and is updated annually as part of the curriculum review process, with department teams determining where course descriptions should be updated to reflect new curriculum and instruction and where courses should be added or deleted.

COURSES ADDED.

AP Business with Personal Finance, grades 9-12, full year, 1.0 credit. The course satisfies 1 credit of the math related graduation requirement. It introduces students to the knowledge and skills needed to grow careers, manage money, and get a head start toward the most popular college major in the U.S. Developed in partnership with college faculty and industry leaders, the yearlong course offers the opportunity to earn college credit and an employer-endorsed credential. Students who participate meet the introductory requirement to have the potential to compete in DECA the following year.

AP Cybersecurity, grades 9-12, full year, 1.0 credit. A yearlong course offering a broad introduction to the field, aligned closely with a college-level introductory cybersecurity course. It replaces and builds upon the previously offered Cybersecurity course. Students learn about common threats and vulnerabilities and how they combine to create risk, how individuals and organizations manage risk, and how risk can be mitigated through a defense-in-depth strategy. They explore vulnerabilities, attacks, mitigations, and detection measures across physical spaces, computer networks, devices, and data and applications, and consider the impact of cybersecurity on individuals, organizations, societies, and governments. Content and skills align with the professional skills outlined in the National Initiative for Cybersecurity Education Workforce Framework. The course is part of the AP Career Kickstart group of courses, designed to accelerate high school students on their paths to in-demand careers, and offers the opportunity to earn an employer-endorsed credential in the cybersecurity field.

AP Precalculus AB, grades 9-12, full year, 1.0 credit. Students must have completed Algebra 2. The course replaces the previously offered Precalculus. Major topics include polynomial, rational, exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions; polar and parametric equations; and the analysis of rates of change. Students may take the AP Precalculus exam and are prepared to take AP Calculus AB.

AP Precalculus BC, grades 9-12, full year, 1.0 credit. Students must have completed Algebra 2. The course replaces the previously offered Honors Precalculus and covers the same major topics plus the additional content of limits and derivatives and vectors. Students may take the AP Precalculus exam and are prepared to take AP Calculus BC.

Career Capstone, grades 11-12, 1 semester, 1/2 credit. Students must be a completer in a business pathway (Finance, BAMO or Marketing). Described as the CTE Professional Capstone, a culminating experience preparing students for college, careers, and real-world professional environments. Students build a professional identity by developing a resume, LinkedIn profile, and digital portfolio showcasing their CTE work, engage in professional-based learning projects that mirror authentic industry challenges, and collaborate with business partners. They refine employability skills through formal interview practice, career coaching, job-shadow opportunities, and reflective activities, graduating with a polished professional toolkit supporting job applications, internships, apprenticeships, and postsecondary pathways.

English 11 Semester 1 is titled Literary Analysis in Reading; Writing about Reading, with students choosing one of three courses, each grade 11, 1 semester, 0.5 credit. English 11 1 - Great American Stories introduces influential and enduring works of American literature through short stories, novels, dramas, and historical texts, exploring identity, freedom, justice, the American Dream, and societal change; texts may include The Great Gatsby, A Raisin in the Sun, and Fences. English 11 1 - Contemporary American Literature examines the contemporary landscape of American literature and themes of freedom, equality, justice, identity, race, immigration, and belonging; texts may include Kindred, King James, and Sweat. English 11 1 - American Dramas and Musicals introduces dramas by American playwrights about the American Dream, American identity, and the American experience in 20th and 21st century plays, along with musicals; texts may include Hamilton, View from the Bridge, and King James. All three include focused sessions on preparing for the SAT.

English 11 Semester 2 is titled Writing with a Purpose and Exploring Mentor Texts, again choosing one of three, each grade 11, 1 semester, 0.5 credit. English 11 2 - Persuasive Writing develops critical thinking, evidence-based argument, and oral presentation, with students forming claims, selecting evidence, addressing counterarguments, and adapting messages to diverse audiences. English 11 2 - Writing Imaginative Fiction develops creative voice through storytelling elements of character, setting, plot, dialogue, and narrative structure, along with poetic techniques such as imagery, metaphor, rhythm, and form, and prepares students to take Creative Writing 2 in senior year. English 11 2 - Writing Personal Memoirs uses close reading of mentor texts including memoirs, personal essays, and narrative nonfiction, teaching sensory detail, structure, reflection, and voice, with each student producing a polished memoir and a collection of shorter writings. All three include focused sessions on writing a rhetorical essay in response to the SAT prompts and creating a working draft of a personal essay.

Mathematics of Tabletop Games, grades 11-12, 1 semester, 0.5 credit. The course qualifies as a 1/2 math-related credit and requires completion of Geometry. Students collaboratively investigate the mathematical foundation of various tabletop games through theorycrafting, experiential observation, and empirical analysis, connecting combinatorics, geometry, probability, game theory, and logic with the medium of tabletop games. The course satisfies 0.5 credit of the math related graduation requirement.

Sports Officiating, grades 9-12, 1 semester, 0.5 credit. Students learn to officiate sports and become certified high school officials upon course completion. The course covers three sports per semester: football, basketball, and a sport of students' choice in the Fall semester; baseball, softball, and soccer in the Spring semester along with a sport of students' choice. Students will earn referrals to local recreational leagues, middle schools, and sub-varsity scholastic assignors.

COURSES REMOVED. The memorandum states that none of these offerings has run in the past five years. Social Studies: Political Science, Stories of Yourself and Others, Psychology 2, Conflicts of the 20th Century, and Philosophy. English: Literature of Suspense, Science Fiction, Voices in Literature, and Modern Shakespeare. Life Skills: Interior Design and Stitchery.

OTHER CHANGES. Achievement Skills III will now be called Integrated Studies III. There are increased math-related and NCAA course approvals. The format of the book changed from PDF to PaperTurn.

2026_340_8_a_full_resolution_requesting_.paragraph: Board of Education resolution, drafted for adoption at the regular meeting of February 24, 2026 at 7:00 p.m., requesting that Oakland Schools Intermediate School District place a regional enhancement millage question before voters. The resolution asks for 1.50 mills for a period of six years, 2026 to 2031 inclusive, at the school election to be held August 4, 2026, under Section 705 of the Revised School Code (MCL 380.705). The attached Exhibit A ballot language states the levy would raise an estimated $125,756,247 if approved and first levied in 2026, with proceeds distributed by Oakland Schools on an equal per-pupil basis to eligible constituent districts and public school academies.
2026_340_8_a_full_resolution_requesting_.page:
**Instrument**
Minutes and resolution of a Regular meeting of the Board of Education of the Troy School District, County of Oakland, State of Michigan, held on the 24th day of February 2026 at 7:00 p.m., local time. The document is a template with blanks for present and absent members, the offering and supporting members, and the ayes and nays.

**Statutory basis**
Section 705 of the Revised School Code of 1976, as amended (MCL 380.705), provides for the levy of a regional enhancement property tax by an intermediate school district at a rate not to exceed 3 mills, to enhance other state and local funding for local school operating purposes, if approved by a majority of the intermediate school district electors. Proceeds are paid to each constituent school district, including eligible public school academies, on a per pupil basis. A constituent school district may request that the ISD submit the question, and the ISD is required to submit it if it receives requests from constituent districts representing a majority of combined membership as of the most recent membership count date.

**Rationale recited**
The intermediate school districts in both Wayne and Macomb County are currently authorized to levy a voter-approved regional enhancement millage, which provides greater student opportunities that may include reduced class sizes, enhanced program offerings, improved school safety, and increased staff retention and attraction, benefits Oakland County currently does not receive. The resolution states that Oakland County residents deserve the opportunity to provide competitive educational opportunities and similar resources to those available in neighboring Wayne and Macomb counties.

**Operative provisions**
1. Requests that Oakland Schools submit to its electors a regional enhancement millage proposal for 1.50 mills for a period of six (6) years, 2026 to 2031 inclusive, at the school election to be held August 4, 2026, in substantially the form of Exhibit A.
2. Approves the Exhibit A ballot wording, subject to revision and finalization by Oakland Schools as necessary.
3. Directs the Superintendent to deliver a certified copy of the resolution to the Secretary of the Board of Education of Oakland Schools.
4. States the resolution is only a request; the proposal will be submitted to voters only if Oakland Schools receives requests from constituent districts representing a majority of combined membership on or before March 31, 2026.
5. Rescinds conflicting resolutions and parts of resolutions.

**Exhibit A ballot language**
Oakland Schools Intermediate School District regional enhancement millage proposal: an increase in the ad valorem tax limitation of 1.5 mills ($1.50 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a period of six (6) years, 2026 to 2031 inclusive, as new additional millage to provide funds to enhance other state and local funding for public school operating purposes. The proposal states the millage would raise an estimated $125,756,247 if approved and first levied in 2026, with YES and NO options. Revenue will be disbursed on an equal per-pupil basis to the listed school districts and public school academies within Oakland Schools boundaries that are eligible under the Revised School Code.

**Certification**
A secretary's certification attests the resolution is a true and complete copy adopted at a Regular meeting held February 24, 2026, conducted with public notice in full compliance with the Open Meetings Act, Act 267, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976.
2026_340_8_a_full_resolution_requesting_.verbose:
Minutes and accompanying resolution for a Regular meeting of the Board of Education of the Troy School District, County of Oakland, State of Michigan, held on the 24th day of February 2026 at 7:00 p.m. local time. The document is presented in template form with blank lines for the members present and absent, for the member offering the resolution and the member supporting it, and for the ayes and nays, and is titled RESOLUTION REQUESTING REGIONAL ENHANCEMENT MILLAGE ELECTION.

WHEREAS CLAUSES. The first clause recites that Section 705 of the Revised School Code of 1976, as amended (MCL 380.705), referred to throughout as Section 705, provides for the levy of a regional enhancement property tax by an intermediate school district at a rate not to exceed 3 mills, for the purpose of enhancing other state and local funding for local school operating purposes, if approved by a majority of the intermediate school district electors. The second clause recites that proceeds of a millage levied pursuant to Section 705 are paid to each constituent school district, including eligible public school academies and referred to as a Constituent School District, by the intermediate school district in an amount calculated on a per pupil basis as provided in Section 705. The third clause recites that a Constituent School District may request an intermediate school district to submit the question of a regional enhancement property tax to the voters at a school election held in each Constituent School District that is a school district. The fourth clause recites that the intermediate school district is required to submit the question to the voters if it receives a request from its Constituent School Districts representing a majority of the combined membership of the Constituent School Districts as of the most recent membership count date.

The fifth clause recites that the intermediate school districts in both Wayne and Macomb County are currently authorized to levy a regional enhancement millage approved by the voters, which provides greater student opportunities that may include, but are not limited to, reduced class sizes, enhanced program offerings, improved school safety, and increased staff retention and attraction, and states these are benefits that Oakland County currently does not receive. The sixth clause states that Oakland County residents deserve the opportunity to provide competitive educational opportunities and similar resources to those available in the neighboring counties of Wayne and Macomb, and that voters should have the ability to determine whether to support these efforts for the benefit of their students. The seventh clause states that the Board of Education has determined that it is in the best interest of the School District to allow voters an opportunity to consider a ballot proposal that enhances educational opportunities by requesting the Oakland Schools Intermediate School District, referred to as Oakland Schools, to submit a regional enhancement millage proposal to the electors at the school election on August 4, 2026, in accordance with Section 705.

RESOLVED PROVISIONS. Paragraph 1 states that the School District requests that Oakland Schools submit to its electors the question of a regional enhancement millage proposal for 1.50 mills for a period of six (6) years, 2026 to 2031 inclusive, at the school election to be held on August 4, 2026, pursuant to a ballot proposal substantially in the form attached as Exhibit A. Paragraph 2 approves the ballot wording substantially in the form attached at Exhibit A, provided that the wording is subject to revision and finalization by Oakland Schools as may be necessary. Paragraph 3 authorizes and directs the Superintendent to deliver a certified copy of the resolution to the Secretary of the Board of Education of Oakland Schools. Paragraph 4 states that the resolution is only a request to Oakland Schools and that the regional enhancement millage proposal will only be submitted to the voters if Oakland Schools receives a request to submit the question from its Constituent School Districts representing a majority of the combined membership of its Constituent School Districts on or before March 31, 2026. Paragraph 5 rescinds all resolutions and parts of resolutions insofar as they conflict with the provisions of this Resolution. The document then records AYES, NAYS, and RESOLUTION DECLARED ADOPTED, with a signature line for the Secretary, Board of Education.

CERTIFICATION. The Secretary of the Board of Education certifies that the foregoing is a true and complete copy of a resolution adopted by the Board of Education of Troy School District, County of Oakland, State of Michigan, at a Regular meeting held on February 24, 2026, and that the meeting was conducted and public notice of the meeting was given pursuant to and in full compliance with the Open Meetings Act, being Act 267, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976, and that the minutes of the meeting were kept and will be or have been made available as required by the Act.

EXHIBIT A - BALLOT LANGUAGE. Headed OAKLAND SCHOOLS INTERMEDIATE SCHOOL DISTRICT, STATE OF MICHIGAN, REGIONAL ENHANCEMENT MILLAGE PROPOSAL. It opens with the statutory explanation that, pursuant to state law, revenue raised by the proposed regional enhancement millage will be collected by the Oakland Schools Intermediate School District and distributed on an equal per-pupil basis to local public school districts and eligible public school academies within the boundaries of the Oakland Schools Intermediate School District.

The proposition reads: Shall the limitation on the amount of ad valorem taxes which may be imposed on taxable property in the Oakland Schools Intermediate School District, State of Michigan, be increased by 1.5 mills ($1.50 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a period of six (6) years, 2026 to 2031, inclusive, as new additional millage to provide funds to enhance other state and local funding for public school operating purposes? This millage would raise an estimated $125,756,247 if approved and first levied in 2026. The ballot then provides YES and NO options.

A closing paragraph states that the revenue from the regional enhancement millage will be disbursed on an equal per-pupil basis to the listed school districts and public school academies within the boundaries of Oakland Schools Intermediate School District which are eligible to receive regional enhancement millage revenue under the Revised School Code; the list itself follows in the source document. The key operative facts are the 1.50 mill rate, the six-year term of 2026 to 2031 inclusive, the August 4, 2026 election date, the March 31, 2026 deadline for the ISD to have collected majority-membership requests, and the estimated first-year yield of $125,756,247 across the ISD.

Resolution Declaring the Necessity to Acquire Highway and Sidewalk Easements and to Authorize Clark Hill PLC to Institute Condemnation Proceedings to Acquire Easements, presented at a special meeting of the Board of Education of the Troy School District, Oakland County, Michigan, held at 4420 Livernois Road, Troy, Michigan 48098-4799 on the 7th day of April 2026 at 7:00 p.m. local time.

**Project**
Construction and operation of the new Smith Middle School on Livernois Road in the City of Troy, including roadway and sidewalk improvements for the benefit of the public and to improve road conditions, safety, mobility and accessibility. The Livernois Road Improvements consist of driveway approaches and a deceleration lane on the east side of Livernois Road, including widening the road, traffic signal and sidewalk improvements.

**Property and owner**
Commonly known as 5836 Livernois Road, Troy, Michigan; Tax Parcel No. 20-10-101-033; owned in fee by Mirza Azam-Ali Baig and Juveria Baig, Husband & Wife. Negotiations with the owner to acquire the easements have not been successful.

Section 11a of Michigan Public Act 451, Public Acts of 1976 (the Revised School Code), MCL 380.11a, gives the district power to acquire interests in real property by condemnation pursuant to the Uniform Condemnation Procedures Act, Public Act 87 of 1980, MCL 213.51 et seq.

Resolution of the Board of Education of the Troy School District, Oakland County, Michigan, titled RESOLUTION DECLARING THE NECESSITY TO ACQUIRE HIGHWAY AND SIDEWALK EASEMENTS AND TO AUTHORIZE CLARK HILL PLC TO INSTITUTE CONDEMNATION PROCEEDINGS TO ACQUIRE EASEMENTS, prepared for a special meeting held at 4420 Livernois Road, Troy, Michigan, 48098-4799 on the 7th day of April, 2026 at 7:00 p.m. local time. The document contains blanks for members present and absent and for the members offering and supporting the resolution.

PROJECT AND NECESSITY. The Troy School District, a Michigan general powers school district acting by and through its Board of Education, is undertaking a project for construction and operation of the new Smith Middle School located on Livernois Road in the City of Troy, Oakland County, Michigan, which includes roadway and sidewalk improvements necessary for the benefit of the public and to improve road conditions, safety, and mobility and accessibility to the school and for road users. As part of the project it is necessary to construct driveway approaches and a deceleration lane on the east side of Livernois Road, including widening the road and making traffic signal and sidewalk improvements, collectively the Livernois Road Improvements. To undertake the project the district must acquire permanent highway and sidewalk easements on, over, across and under real property owned in fee by Mirza Azam-Ali Baig and Juveria Baig, Husband & Wife, commonly known as 5836 Livernois Road, Troy, Michigan, Tax Parcel No. 20-10-101-033. Negotiations with the owner to acquire the easements have not been successful.

LEGAL AUTHORITY. Pursuant to Sections 11a of Michigan Public Act 451, Public Acts of 1976, the Revised School Code, as amended, MCL 380.11a, the district has power to acquire interests in real property by condemnation pursuant to the Uniform Condemnation Procedures Act, Public Act 87 of 1980, as amended, MCL 213.51 et seq. The UCPA establishes procedures for taking property by eminent domain. The district reserves the right to bring federal or state cost recovery actions against the owner for costs incurred as a result of the release of hazardous or toxic substances or materials which may have occurred on the easement. The district intends to present a good faith written offer to acquire the easements in exchange for just compensation based on an appraisal by a state certified appraiser, and if the owner rejects the offer, Clark Hill PLC is authorized to institute a condemnation lawsuit.

RESOLVED PROVISIONS. Paragraph 1 declares the project a public improvement and the acquisition of the easements necessary and essential for the Livernois Road Improvements, which benefit the public and improve public safety. Paragraph 2 authorizes the Superintendent of Schools, or in his absence the Deputy Superintendent of Business Affairs, to take all action and execute all documents necessary under the Revised School Code and UCPA to acquire the easements, record the Statement of Necessity and Declaration of Taking of Private Property in substantial form as set forth in Exhibit A, retain qualified appraisers or other consultants to determine just compensation, make good faith written offers to property owners, enter negotiations, reach agreements as to just compensation, and initiate proceedings in the Oakland County Circuit Court. Paragraph 3 authorizes the Deputy Superintendent of Schools of Business Affairs to establish an escrow account with First American Title Company for the specific amounts estimated to be just compensation. Paragraph 4 retains Clark Hill PLC, or in the event of a conflict another firm the Superintendent may select, to initiate condemnation proceedings in the Oakland County Circuit Court. Paragraph 5 authorizes the Deputy Superintendent of Schools of Business Affairs to select a real estate appraiser or other consultants, considering estimated appraisal cost, timing of services, professional services, and expert witness qualifications. Paragraph 6 reserves the district's right to bring federal or state cost recovery actions for hazardous or toxic substance releases. Signature blocks record YEAS, NAYS and ABSTAIN by members, with certification by the Secretary of the Board of Education that the resolution was duly adopted at a special meeting held on the 7th day of April, 2026, conducted with public notice in full compliance with the Open Meetings Act, Act 267, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976.

EXHIBIT A, STATEMENT OF PUBLIC NECESSITY AND DECLARATION OF TAKING OF PRIVATE PROPERTY.
